top_comments.text: STOP TRYING, CASSIE! Here's why: Decades ago, I worked in a community mental health center's speech and language pathology department. I was in my twenties, finding my way as a young adult. I was struggling and went downstairs to the psychology department for some guidance. I got a strong suggestion, and as I was heading back to my office I said, "Thank you, I'll try." "Whoa!" said the psychologist. "Pick up that tissue box. Now TRY to throw it at me. Don't actually throw it at me; just TRY to throw it at me." What a great lesson! From that day forward, I no longer use that word. It's a trap word. Instead, I either say "I will" or "I won't." I'm 77 now. I've been on a ketogenic journey 12 years and have steadily kept off 35 of the 40 pounds I initially lost. 1. If you’re a male, stand down. Female hormones are no joke. Sit down. Go talk to Larry, fine, but leave Cassie alone.

One bad reaction to a medication is enough to make some people risk-averse to taking prescriptions. Accept the “no thank you” and move on.
3. Gene expression research is proving time and time again that a lot of people who don’t struggle with weight have genes that make it easier for them. You can’t easily change your eye color without contacts. You can’t change how your genes express. You can fight against it, but don’t compare your “I just cut my portions a little and take one extra walk and I’m fine” with others’ “I already eat so little and walk so much but nothing changes” lived experience.
